To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

allopurinil treatment in pregnant sows increases brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and the post-synaptic marker postsynaptic density-95 (PSD95) in the dorsal hippocampi of both low and normal birth-weight piglets.

allopurinil, an antioxidant treatment given in late pregnancy to pregnant sows, has a protective effect on the levels of plasticity markers BDNF, CREB and PSD95 in low and normal weight birth weight piglets.
“Allopurinol, an antioxidant drug, given daily in the late gestation to sows has a protective effect on brain plasticity makers in their piglets.”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long-term effects of prenatal ALLO treatment on neuronal plasticity in LBW piglet hippocampi.
the development of novel, noninvasive methods of prenatal diagnosis of fetal growth restriction (FGR).
the effects of allopurinolic treatment in the last trimesters of pregnancy on brain plasticity in piglets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
allopurinil is not an effective treatment for LBW piglets.
allopurinolic treatment in the third trimester of gestation in sows is a promising approach for improving brain function in LBW piglet offspring.
the antioxidant treatment with allopurinil has a positive influence on the development of the hippocampus of LBW and NBV piglets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the antioxidant allopurinil treatment given to the mother pig during the last trimester of pregnancy has a protective effect on the newborn piglets, especially on low birth weight piglets, by reducing oxidative stress and by increasing brain plasticity markers.

ALLO treatment given during the last trimester of gestation increases levels of plasticity markers and improves the balance of excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmission in the dorsal hippocampi of LBW piglets, thus providing a neuroprotective effect.

ALLO treatment given to the mother in the last trimesters of pregnancy increases levels of BDNTr, pCREB and PSD95 in LBWs and normalises levels in the NBWs, which is a protective effect on plasticity markers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
allopurinil is a promising treatment for reducing the risk of brain damage in LBW neonates and may be useful for other neurodevelopmental disorders as well.
allopurinil treatment in the last trimesters of pregnancy might have a positive effect on neuronal plastic markers in LBW piglet brain.
allopuriniol, an antioxidant, can increase the levels of plasticity markers, which are important for brain development.
